source_metadata.title: COVID-19 and Spontaneous Pneumomediastinum: A case series
source_metadata.design: descriptive case series (3 patients; no comparator group)

atoms.canonical_statement: The report describes three hospitalized patients with COVID-19 who developed pneumomediastinum during their hospital course, emphasizing occurrence despite non-smoking history and absence of positive-pressure ventilation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we describe three cases involving Hispanic males with COVID-19 all of whom developed pneumomediastinum during their hospital course.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors present a case series from a county hospital in Long Island, New York, involving three patients with pneumomediastinum in the absence of positive-pressure ventilation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Presented below is a case series from a county hospital in Long Island, New York on three patients diagnosed with pneumomediastinum in the absence of positive pressure ventilation.

atoms.canonical_statement: All three reported patients were Hispanic men, non-smokers, had no underlying pulmonary disease reported, were not receiving positive-pressure ventilation, and developed pneumomediastinum at least two weeks after hospital admission.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: they all involve non-smokers with no underlying pulmonary disease, the absence of positive pressure ventilation and delayed presentation (two weeks or more) after hospital admission.

population.label: Three hospitalized Hispanic male COVID-19 patients

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 was a 51-year-old obese Hispanic man, a non-smoker with no significant medical history, admitted after three days of cough, chills, and dyspnea.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 51-year-old obese Hispanic male, non-smoker with no significant medical history was admitted with three days of cough, chills and dyspnea.

atoms.canonical_statement: At admission, Case 1 had temperature 103°F and oxygen saturation 88% while receiving 15 L/min by non-rebreather mask.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On admission, his temperature was 103 degrees Fahrenheit and oxygen saturation was 88% on non-rebreather mask (NRB) 15 L/min.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 had a reported PaO2:FiO2 ratio of 68 in severe ARDS secondary to SARS-CoV-2 viral pneumonia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: with a PaO2:FiO2 ratio of 68.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 admission laboratory values included CRP 10.1 mg/dL, LDH 439 U/L, D-dimer 0.40 ug/mL, and ferritin 489 ng/mL; the white blood cell count was reported as normal.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: C-reactive protein elevated at 10.1 mg/dL, lactate dehydrogenase elevated at 439 U/L, D-dimer elevated at 0.40 ug/mL and ferritin elevated at 489 ng/mL.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 received hydroxychloroquine, azithromycin, methylprednisolone, tocilizumab, and convalescent plasma during hospitalization.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: He was treated with a course of hydroxychloroquine, azithromycin, and methylprednisolone. He received tocilizumab and convalescent plasma.

concept.text: COVID-19-directed pharmacotherapy (hydroxychloroquine, azithromycin, methylprednisolone, tocilizumab, convalescent plasma)

atoms.canonical_statement: Pneumomediastinum was detected in Case 1 on hospital day 15, when sudden chest pain and worsening hypoxemia occurred; chest radiography also showed a small right apical pneumothorax.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On day 15 of his hospitalization, he developed sudden chest pain and worsening hypoxemia. Chest x-ray showed right sided apical pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: On day 15 of his hospitalization, he developed sudden chest pain and worsening hypoxemia. Chest x-ray showed right sided apical pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum.

atoms.canonical_statement: Figure 1 shows pneumomediastinum and a small right apical pneumothorax in Case 1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Pneumomediastinum (arrow) with small right apical pneumothorax (notched arrow)

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 underwent chest-tube placement with improved oxygenation; pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum resolved, the tube was removed, and he was discharged to rehabilitation on 3 L/min nasal-cannula oxygen.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: He had a chest tube placed with improvement in his oxygenation. His pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum resolved after which chest tube was removed.

atoms.canonical_statement: At 8-week CT follow-up, Case 1 had peripheral ground-glass opacities with bronchiectasis and no significant underlying bullous lung disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: He had a CT thorax done 8 weeks later which showed peripheral ground glass opacities with bronchiectasis. No significant underlying bullous lung disease was noted.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 was a 37-year-old obese Hispanic man, a non-smoker with no significant medical history, admitted after five days of cough, fever, and dyspnea.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 37-year-old obese, Hispanic male, non-smoker with no significant medical history was admitted with five days of cough, fever, and dyspnea.

atoms.canonical_statement: At admission, Case 2 was afebrile with heart rate 108/min, respiratory rate 31/min, and oxygen saturation 92% while receiving 15 L/min by non-rebreather mask.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On admission, he was afebrile, tachycardic with a heart rate of 108 beats per minute, tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 31 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation was 92% on NRB 15 L/min.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 had a reported PaO2:FiO2 ratio of 80 in severe ARDS secondary to SARS-CoV-2 viral pneumonia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: with a PaO2:FiO2 ratio of 80.

atoms.canonical_statement: Pneumomediastinum was detected in Case 2 on hospital day 14 while persistent hypoxemia required 15 L/min by non-rebreather mask plus 6 L/min nasal cannula.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On day 14 of his hospitalization, he had persistent hypoxemia requiring 15 L/min NRB and 6 L/min nasal cannula. Chest x-ray showed pneumomediastinum.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: On day 14 of his hospitalization, he had persistent hypoxemia requiring 15 L/min NRB and 6 L/min nasal cannula. Chest x-ray showed pneumomediastinum.

atoms.canonical_statement: CT in Case 2 showed complete ground-glass opacification of both lungs, diffuse pneumomediastinum, and a small amount of pneumopericardium, without significant underlying bullous lung disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CT thorax done which showed complete ground glass opacification of bilateral lungs, diffuse pneumomediastinum, and small amount of pneumopericardium. No significant underlying bullous lung disease was noted.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 was managed conservatively, had slowly decreasing oxygen requirements, and was discharged after 27 days on 2 L/min nasal-cannula oxygen; follow-up chest radiography showed persistent pneumomediastinum with improved bilateral consolidations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: He was discharged home after a 27-day hospitalization on 2 L/min nasal cannula oxygen. He was followed up in a pulmonary clinic with continued improvement in his symptoms.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 3 was a 34-year-old Hispanic man, a non-smoker with no significant medical history, admitted after two weeks of nonproductive cough, diarrhea, non-bloody non-bilious emesis, and subjective fevers.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 34-year-old Hispanic male, non-smoker with no significant medical history was admitted with two-week history of non-productive cough, diarrhea, non-bloody, non-bilious emesis and subjective fevers.

atoms.canonical_statement: At admission, Case 3 was afebrile with heart rate 140/min and oxygen saturation 90% on room air and 99% on 4 L/min nasal cannula.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On admission, he was afebrile, tachycardic with a heart rate of 140 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation 90% on room air and 99% on 4 L/min nasal cannula.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 3 had a reported PaO2:FiO2 ratio of 59 in severe ARDS secondary to SARS-CoV-2 viral pneumonia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: with a PaO2:FiO2 ratio of 59.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 3 admission findings included lymphocytopenia 6%, CRP 26.9 mg/dL, LDH 353 U/L, D-dimer 0.66 ug/mL, ferritin 478 ng/mL, and a normal white blood cell count.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: lymphocytopenia of 6%. C-reactive protein elevated at 26.9 mg/dL, lactate dehydrogenase elevated at 353 U/L, D-dimer elevated at 0.66 ug/mL and ferritin elevated at 478 ng/mL.

atoms.canonical_statement: CT pulmonary angiography in Case 3 showed patchy bilateral pulmonary consolidation without pulmonary embolic filling defects and without evidence of bullous lung disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: revealed patchy bilateral pulmonary consolidation and no evidence of filling defects. There was also no evidence of bullous lung disease.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 3 had worsening hypoxia requiring 15 L/min by non-rebreather mask plus 6 L/min nasal cannula; on hospital day 18 he had persistent hypoxemia with worsening respiratory distress and refused intubation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On day 18 of his hospitalization, he had persistent hypoxemia with worsening respiratory distress. Patient refused intubation.

atoms.canonical_statement: Pneumomediastinum was detected in Case 3 on hospital day 36 and was attributed by the authors as likely secondary to violent coughing.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On hospital day 36, he developed pneumomediastinum (Fig. 3) likely secondary to violent coughing

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 3 improved with conservative management; predischarge chest radiography showed resolution of pneumomediastinum and improved bilateral consolidations, and he was discharged home after six weeks on 2 L/min nasal-cannula oxygen.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Chest x-ray done prior to discharge revealed significant improvement in bilateral consolidations and resolution of pneumomediastinum. After six weeks since hospital admission, the patient was discharged home on 2 L/min nasal cannula.

atoms.canonical_statement: The discussion describes pneumomediastinum as arising when increased alveolar pressure causes alveolar rupture and air tracks along the perivascular sheath toward the mediastinum.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Pneumomediastinum is thought to be caused by an increase in pressure in the alveoli, due to various etiologies, which in turn causes the alveoli to rupture.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors characterize pneumomediastinum as a rare complication of COVID-19.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Current research shows that pneumomediastinum is a rare complication of COVID-19.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors emphasize that their three cases lacked prior risk factors for pneumomediastinum and were not treated with positive-pressure ventilation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients in our case series had no prior risk factors for developing pneumomediastinum and were not being treated by positive pressure ventilation.

atoms.canonical_statement: The discussion notes potential complications of pneumomediastinum including tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade, significant subcutaneous emphysema, and pneumorrhachis, with possible cardiorespiratory compromise.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: this can potentially lead to further problems including tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade, significant subcutaneous emphysema, or pneumorrhachis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommend considering pneumomediastinum in the differential diagnosis when patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia develop new chest pain and worsening shortness of breath.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: pneumomediastinum should be in the differential diagnosis in patients with severe SARS-COV2 pneumonia, who develop new symptoms of chest pain and worsening shortness of breath.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that repeat chest radiographs should be obtained in these patients to recognize pneumomediastinum.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Repeat chest radiographs should be taken in these patients to recognize pneumomediastinum.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that conservative management is usually the treatment of choice for pneumomediastinum, while cautioning that cardiorespiratory compromise can occur.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Conservative management usually is the treatment of choice, although cardiorespiratory compromise can occur and caution should be warranted.

atoms.canonical_statement: The exact mechanism by which pneumomediastinum occurs in COVID-19 patients remained unclear in this report.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The exact mechanism for which pneumomediastinum occurs in COVID-19 patients still remains unclear.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors call for further research on pneumomediastinum in COVID-19.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Further research in this area should be conducted.
